what: The builder ran a long series of grep, cat and old-script reads without a kb_search, and the kb guard warned about it about fifteen times in this chunk.
why: Builder reached for session scripts (.scratch/r*.sh), generated sources and grep first, despite the standing kb-first rule.
workaround: Builder kept going on source reads; no kb consult until the guard warnings and later migration steps.

what: CompanyService and ApprovalService did not compile: getCompanyRole, getCompanyAdmin and getPoRequired return plain values, but the builder called orElse on them, then patched with sed.
why: Builder assumed Optional getters for every attribute. The catalog data-access guide says required attributes get plain getters and optional ones get Optional; the builder did not check it before writing code.
workaround: sed edits to ApprovalService and CompanyService to drop orElse; rebuild passed.

what: judo CLI query rejects several field selections: Access target needs a subselection, target{fqn} is not a field, TransferObjectType attributes{...} is not a field, binding needs a subselection, Operation isStatic and ActorType principal{fqn} are not fields.
why: The CLI query schema is not documented in the catalog in a form the builder could use; each guess cost a round trip.
workaround: Builder listed names with grep over fq() output and read the valid-field list printed in each error.
proposed_target: judo CLI query esm (field names and subselection rules)

what: judo query ui MenuItemAccess failed because MenuItemAccess is an esm type, not a ui type; the builder had to fall back to query esm for menu items.
why: Type names for query ui and query esm differ and the CLI error lists valid types without saying which lane holds menus.
workaround: Used query esm MenuItemAccess for the menu list.
proposed_target: judo CLI query ui (type lookup for menu items)

what: Operation buttons and some fields were rejected by update --add feature with the message feature not placeable here, while the same operations existed as UI elements under their own FQN.
why: Unverified: the chunk shows the CLI rule but not the documented route for placing an operation button. The builder did not kb_search this before trying variants.
workaround: Builder updated the generated button element directly by FQN (label, hiddenBy) and did not place it via --add feature.

what: Generated customer frontend fails Biome with a duplicate import: ShopMessage and ShopMessageStored are imported twice when an operation returns a mapped type.
why: Generator emits duplicate imports for a mapped operation output (already recorded as GAPS R8-5, referenced in the checkout hook comment).
workaround: Builder removed the output parameter from the invite operations (-u output), so the generator stopped emitting the import.

what: Build failed with XMI ID COLLISION errors on Admin TabularReferenceField link actions, then ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition, after new relation-field and action edits.
why: Cause not stated in the chunk. The collision names the Admin TabularReferenceField link actions, and the builder had just added a TabularReferenceField (OrderInfo_Form returns). Not confirmed.
workaround: Builder deleted and re-added table operations and rebuilt; the next build passed after the output change.

what: Frontend Maven step fails at pnpm install with ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS (core-js-pure, esbuild), so the format step fails and the build stops; the same message is in an earlier build log.
why: pnpm blocks dependency build scripts that are not approved; the generated build does not approve them.
workaround: Builder ran npx biome directly instead of pnpm run format.

what: Builder ran biome format and check with --write on the generated customer frontend source, which is generated code.
why: Builder used the formatter as a fix for the pnpm failure instead of approving the build or leaving generated files alone (standing rule: never patch generated files).
workaround: Rebuilt with judo.sh build; build passed at L4750.

what: Running mvn compile in application/app failed in the PSM generator with: there are manual changes in the generated files, discard them or add them to .generator-ignore.
why: Generator checksum guard sees changed generated files. Likely related to c08-09 but not proven in the chunk.
workaround: Builder ran judo.sh generate-root and judo.sh build instead, which passed.

what: discard --force threw away unsaved model edits from a fill run after an error, and the builder had to rebuild those edits.
why: Builder ran fill and an update in one step, then discarded instead of saving first; the edits were not saved.
workaround: Builder re-ran the feature and label edits in later scripts.

what: Invitation key blueprint assumes an anonymous actor, so the invitee cannot accept the key without a Keycloak account. The builder adds sign-up first, then key entry, and shows the key in the admin table and log.
why: Chunk does not show why anonymous acceptance was not used. GAPS R13-3 records the decision as platform limit with no mail server.
workaround: Key shown in the open-invitations table and logged; invitee signs up, then enters key on Join a company; acceptance checks key, expiry and e-mail and deletes the invitation in one transaction.

what: Company members are CustomerAccount rows inside the existing Customer actor (company relation, companyRole BUYER or APPROVER, companyAdmin flag). No third actor.
why: One user has one organization and a small fixed role set, which is the user-with-organization-and-role case. A third actor would add a Keycloak client and a frontend module. B2C must keep working.

what: Model changes went through the F52 migration route: pg_dump before the step, a base model from before the round, a generated migration, a hand-written backfill setting companyAdmin false on existing customers, then execute. No database wipe; 251 customer rows kept.
why: Orchestrator rule for every model change after round 12; a required new flag needs a backfill.

what: Migration command syntax (judo-rdbms-schema:generate and :execute) was recalled from session history with the recall tool instead of kb_search.
why: Builder reached for session memory rather than the catalog schema-evolution guide.
workaround: Used the recalled command; it worked.

what: Generated after-changeset for the new columns and tables contained an unresolved context variable, so the builder rewrote the file by hand and replaced the variable with sed.
why: Unclear from chunk whether the generator is expected to leave this for the developer. The builder states the generator writes the file empty and the backfill is hand-written.
workaround: Hand-written changeset; sed substitution of the context value; execute passed and counts checked by psql.

what: Builder states that the generator adds every new column as a plain nullable column, so an existing row gets NULL and a required flag needs a backfill.
why: Builder read this from the kb (migration-backfill-default-where-null) and applied it.

what: After the build, app start logged NoClassDefFoundError for hu/blackbelt/epsilon/runtime/execution/contexts/EolExecutionContext and Could not find compatible schema model; the same error appears in the round 12 start log.
why: Not resolved in this chunk. Looks like a platform runtime or classpath issue, not a model error.
workaround: Builder kept going; the app answered HTTP 200 on the admin URL.

what: Playwright checks typed 5000 into a number field that shows 5,000, and a Create button matched two elements in a dialog (strict mode).
why: Test design: the test asserted the raw value, not the formatted display; the dialog had two Create buttons.
workaround: Tests now compare the formatted value and use .last() on the dialog Create button.

what: After the buyer joins with the key, the My company menu does not appear until the shell starts again.
why: Builder comment says menu entries are decided from the principal read at shell start, so a page change does not refresh them.
workaround: Post-join hook calls window.location.assign on the start URL to reload the shell.

what: Generated action group shows the first three actions; Request a quote sits under the Actions menu in the cart, so the test must open the menu.
why: Platform behaviour of the generated action group (featured actions), not a bug.
workaround: Test opens Actions and clicks the menu item. Not hidden or patched.

what: Quote lines and company price rows open on their own nested page. Invite a member is enabled only after the company prices are stored with Update.
why: Platform generated edit-page behaviour; Admin.quotes also needed updateable for the discount field.
workaround: Tests open the nested page, edit, Update, Back; Admin.quotes set updateable true.

what: Table pages keep every run's rows and show ten per page, so a test could not find the company or quote it had just created.
why: Test design: the tests relied on the first page of a list that grows with each run.
workaround: Tests filter by name or number with openAddAndApplyFilters.

what: Full customer suite ran with parallel workers: customers shared one cart and one seeded stock, so stock reached zero and tests interfered. Builder reset stock with a direct SQL UPDATE.
why: Test isolation: shared fixtures and parallel workers. Not a code bug.
workaround: Direct SQL reset of stock; new rule: run new spec with --grep @smoke, full suites once, serial.

what: Final full customer suite run was aborted by the tool (Command aborted), so the round's full-suite result is not in this chunk.
why: Cause not shown in the chunk.

what: A sed -i edit to level7.spec.ts replaced a line with the placeholder XX, causing a ReferenceError until fixed.
why: Builder used an unsafe sed pattern on a source file.
workaround: Replaced XX with the intended line in the next step.

what: Several bash commands ran in the same parallel batch as a read of their output, so the read ran first and returned ENOENT.
why: Builder issued bash and read calls without waiting for the write to finish.
workaround: Re-ran the read after the command.

what: Browser snapshot selectors failed on text and role names (Products not found by text or by role name) during admin exploration.
why: Selector and snapshot mismatch in the agent browser tool; not verified further.
workaround: Used snapshot refs and waits instead.

what: About eight full generate and build cycles of two to three minutes each, plus sleeps of up to four minutes, for small label and feature changes.
why: Each label or feature change needs regeneration and build; no faster loop is used in the chunk.
workaround: Batched edits into one rebuild script (rebuild.sh).

what: Money in admin tables and forms (company credit values, quote lines, quote total) uses derived ...Label strings such as '5.00 EUR' instead of the Price component. The numeric fields stay for sums.
why: Same own pattern as round 12 (R12). The orchestrator standing rule asks for the shared Price component in cart, order and card grid, which the builder did use.

what: Companies, members, invitations with key, join by key, company admin invite and role change; the level 7 test for F55 passed.
Company price list with Product.companyPrices; the shared Price component shows the company price, a company without a list sees the list price; the level 7 test passed.
Quantity price tiers (Product.tiers, PriceTierInfo) with unit price switching at 10 and 50; the level 7 test passed.
Checkout branches to PENDING_APPROVAL when the order exceeds the remaining credit; the test passed in the level 7 run with six passing.
Approve and reject operations via ApprovalService; negative test (buyer cannot approve own order) passed in the level 7 run.
Quote and QuoteLine with request a quote from the cart, admin discount and offer, convert to order; the quote test passed after many test fixes.
Purchase order number on SalesOrder and checkout input, required when the company sets poRequired; column added by migration. No separate test result seen in the chunk.
